results.title: Announcement for Ramadan-Shawwal 1447 / 2026 - Fiqh Council of North America
results.author: Dr. Zulfiqar Ali Shah
highlights:
Ramadan 1447 AH: The Astronomical New Moon will be born before sunset on Tuesday, February 17, 2026. So, the first day of Ramadan is Wednesday, February 18, 2026, inshā’Allāh. Tarāwīḥ prayer will start on Tuesday night.
...
Based on the ECFR criteria mentioned, declaring Wednesday, February 18 as the first day of Ramadan is fully consistent with our methodology. On the evening of Tuesday, February 17, all three foundational elements of our adopted criteria are satisfied:
...
1. The moon is born before sunset on February 17.

2. Moonset occurs after sunset in Makkah and throughout the western hemisphere, including California.

3. The geometric visibility thresholds are met westward: lunar elongation reaches or exceeds 8 degrees, and lunar altitude reaches or exceeds 5 degrees above the horizon.
...
This explains the hesitation expressed by Diyanet (Turkey) and, following it, the European Council of Fatwa and Research, which concluded that despite meeting the geometric thresholds, the moon is not practically sightable anywhere on Earth on February 17. Consequently, much of the world may begin Ramadan on the evening of Wednesday, February 18 (and fasting on Thursday, February 19), when the moon will be older, brighter, and easily visible across wide regions.
...
At this point, the decision rests with us. Declaring the start of Ramadan on the evening of February 17 is defensible, fully compliant with our long-standing criteria, and consistent with our previous announcements. It also ensures the completion of 30 days of fasting without risk of omission. However, it carries the possibility that we may be among the very few—or even the only—communities beginning Ramadan that night, potentially placing us at variance with the ECFR, whose criteria we have historically followed. Despite this possibility, we have decided to stick with the long-standing method and have established the dates of Ramadan and ʿEid al-Fitr based on the original ECFR criteria. May Allah (swt) keep us on the right path and accept our fasting and prayers. Ameen.

results.title: Ramadan 2026: When Does Ramadan Begin and End?
highlights:
This year, the holy month of Ramadan begins at the first sighting of the crescent Moon on the evening of Tuesday, February 17, 2026. Learn about how—and why—Ramadan is observed.
...
This year, Ramadan is expected to begin at sundown on Tuesday, February 17, and end at sundown on Wednesday, March 18. The final evening of Ramadan consists of a celebration called Eid al-Fitr, when the traditional month-long fast is ended with a feast.
...
The exact beginning and ending times of the month of Ramadan are based on the sighting of the first crescent Moon on the last night of the eighth month (Sha’ban). Specifically, Ramadan is said to begin at the first observance of the crescent Moon over Mecca, Saudi Arabia (or on a date predetermined by astronomical calculation). Because of this, start and end dates are not set in stone and may vary by a day.

The Islamic calendar is lunar; each month begins when the first crescent of a new moon is sighted. The Islamic year consists of 12 lunar cycles and is 10 to 11 days shorter than the solar year. As the Islamic calendar does not use intercalation, Ramadan migrates throughout the seasons. The Islamic day starts after sunset. The estimated start and end dates for Ramadan, based on the Umm al-Qura calendar of Saudi Arabia, are:
...
Ramadan dates between 2024 and 2028
...
| AH | First day (CE/ AD) | Last day (CE/ AD) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1445 | 11 March 2024 | 9 April 2024 |
| 1446 | 1 March 2025 | 29 March 2025 |
| 1447 | 18 February 2026 | 19 March 2026 |
| 1448 | 8 February 2027 | 8 March 2027 |
| 1449 | 28 January 2028 | 25 February 2028 |
...
Many Muslims insist on the local physical sighting of the moon to mark the beginning of Ramadan, but others use the calculated time of the new moon or the Saudi Arabian declaration to determine the start of the month. Since the new moon is not in the same state at the same time globally, Ramadan's beginning and ending depend on what lunar sightings are received in each location. As a result, Ramadan dates vary in different countries, but usually by only a day. This is due to the cycles of the moon; the moon may not qualify as a waxing crescent, which delineates the change in months, at sundown in one location but later meet it in another location. Astronomical projections that approximate the start of Ramadan are available.

results.title: Saudi Arabia sets Wednesday start to Ramadan 2026
results.author: Zac Crellin  Journalist and editor based in Germany zacrellin
highlights:
Saudi Arabia sets Wednesday start to Ramadan 2026
...
Hundreds of millions of Muslims around the world are preparing to fast for the holy month of Ramadan after Saudi astronomers sighted the new moon on Tuesday evening.
...
However, countries differ on the exact start date, with some expecting Ramadan to begin on Wednesday and others on Thursday.
...
After Saudi astronomers sighted the new moon on Tuesday, the royal court announced that the first day of Ramadan would fall on Wednesday — a decision that tends to be followed in other majority-Muslim countries.
...
Saudi Arabia's Gulf neighbors Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates also announced that Ramadan would start on Wednesday.
...
Meanwhile, religious authorities in some countries including Jordan, Oman, Syria and Turkey said Ramadan would instead begin on Thursday.
...
For example, the Sharjah Academy for Astronomy, Space Sciences and Technology in the UAE as well as Oman's Main Committee for Moon Sighting both said the moon would not be visible until Wednesday night, and that Ramadan should therefore begin on Thursday.
...
"On Tuesday 17 February 2026, the crescent moon is astronomically impossible to see, whether by high powered telescopes or by the unaided eye anywhere in the Middle East — indeed, in the whole of Asia, Africa, or Europe," Imad Ahmed, founder and director of the New Crescent Society told Middle East Eye.
...
Saudi authorities have in previous years also declared the start of Ramadan despite other astronomers claiming that moon sightings were impossible.
